title: REFACTOR bot-ai-system into per-verb strategy modules (file grew to ~960 LOC across S220-S225)
intent: User feedback 2026-06-02: 'bot-ai-system сильно разраслась, нужно сделать отдельные стратегии или ещё как-то разделить'. The file passed 960 LOC after S220-S225 stacked five tactical-verb decision branches (KICK / REMOTE / SHIELD / PIERCE / THROW) + S225 player anticipation on top of the original S82 brain. Single-file inline detection helpers (findKickOpportunity, wouldKillEnemyAt, countSoftBlocksInLine, maybeFireBotThrow, predictNextCell, anticipatedPlayerCell) all live in the closure now — readable per individual story but the cumulative `shouldDropBomb` + `fixedUpdate` are getting tangled.
rationale: Source: user request during S225 ship. The bot-ai code is the canonical example of 'works, ships features fast, but the next contributor hits a wall'. CLAUDE.md says 'prefer small patches with verification over broad refactors' so the verb-branch stack was intentional; now the cleanup story is the natural follow-up. Risk: bot-vs-bot demo snapshot is the regression baseline + has bitten us twice already (S210 + S213); the refactor must preserve every decision branch byte-for-byte under the same RNG sequence.
acceptanceHints: DESIRED SHAPE: split into per-verb strategy modules + a thin orchestrator. Pseudo-tree:
anticipation.ts        — predictNextCell + anticipatedPlayerCell + per-player track ring (S225)
should-drop-bomb.ts    — composes the tactical branches + aggression dice
create-system.ts       — the public createKaboomBotAISystem entry — wires the strategies
index.ts re-exports the public surface (createKaboomBotAISystem + the helpers tests depend on).
- Existing 55+ unit tests stay green untouched (re-import paths only if names move).
- demo-30s snapshot fingerprint stays byte-identical. If it diverges, the refactor is wrong, not the snapshot — fix the order-of-operations.
- Same per-system seeded RNG instance threads through every tactical helper that calls `rng.next()`. No new rng streams.

- shouldDropBomb's BRANCH ORDER stays exactly the same: remote > shield > pierce > adjacent soft block > boost-empty. Reordering breaks determinism for the demo snapshot even if the rule logic stays identical.
EXPORT CONTRACT: each tactical module exports a `function tryX(world, botId, pos, stats) -> boolean | undefined` shape so `shouldDropBomb` reads as:
OPTIONAL — extract the kick-direction override the same way as `tryKickOverride(world, botId, pos, stats) -> Direction | undefined`.
- All current unit tests (bot-ai-system, bot-acceleration, bot-kick, bot-remote-place, bot-shield-place, bot-pierce-place, bot-throw) continue to import from the public re-export and pass.

- One new file-size budget test (kaboom-crew/tests/unit/bot-ai-file-size.test.ts) asserts the orchestrator file stays under, say, 200 LOC after the refactor — prevents the next contributor from re-growing the centre.
- Renaming helpers (keep tryRemote, tryShield, tryPierce one-to-one with existing names).
- New gameplay behaviour. Pure code organisation.
- Engine-side changes (bomb-block-system / bomb-kick-system stay where they are).
